key_insight: You can validly compare LLM safety without labeled benchmarks by auditing models under a precisely specified contract (scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling configuration, rerun budget); scores are meaningful only inside that fixed audit context.
problem_solved: How to produce defensible comparative safety evidence for candidate language models when no ground-truth labeled benchmark exists for the target language, sector, or regulatory regime.
method: Formalize the 'benchmarkless comparative safety scoring' setting and define the contract elements required to interpret an audit as deployment evidence.
Use scenario-based audits that combine a scenario pack, rubric, designated auditor and judge, controlled sampling configuration, and a fixed rerun budget to generate comparative scores.
Replace reliance on ground-truth labels with a protocol that quantifies comparisons and uncertainty under the fixed contract so results are reproducible and interpretable only within that scope.
impact: Allows practitioners to run defensible, repeatable safety comparisons before labeled benchmarks exist while making explicit the limits of those comparisons—enabling better deployment decisions and clearer audit documentation.
visual_elements: Contract diagram showing the required elements (scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling config, rerun budget) as linked components
Audit pipeline flowchart: generate scenarios → apply rubric → auditor/judge evaluation → aggregate comparative scores
Comparison chart illustrating model scores across the same contract and how scores change if contract elements vary (sensitivity)
Checklist/badge graphic that emphasizes: 'Valid only under this contract' to convey the scoped validity of results
paper_title: When No Benchmark Exists: Validating Comparative LLM Safety Scoring Without Ground-Truth Labels
paper_authors: Sushant Gautam, Finn Schwall, Annika Willoch Olstad, Fernando Vallecillos Ruiz, Birk Torpmann-Hagen
